properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent, and no option is preferred.

THE OBSERVATION, which unifies three separately-filed asks plus one this session hit unprompted. reflow2's relation vocabulary is rich and every relation requires BOTH ENDS TO BE MODELLED NODES. When the natural other end is not design content, the user must first mint a node whose only purpose is to be an edge endpoint.

FOUR SIGHTINGS, three of them somebody else's:

① F-18 (hxm_program, 2026-09-09→10). `record_finding(caused_by=…)` needs an existing node, and a CODE DEFECT'S NATURAL CAUSE IS A FILE. For each of three defects: `add_artifact` for the file, then `realizes` something "so it is not an island", then `create_edge CAUSES`. Their words: "three new Artifact nodes this session PURELY TO CARRY A CAUSE".

② O-10 (same report). The failure CLASS named by root-cause step ⑥ has nowhere to live but prose. Three beamline incidents shared one class — a device assuming screen or plugin state that nothing sets or checks — and the only link between them is a MITIGATES edge from a later requirement. The fourth recurrence will be found by guessing search terms.

③ O-09 (same report). An Artifact in another repo carries an ad-hoc location string ("hextools:src/…, branch X, PR N, head sha") and `reconcile_artifacts` can never examine it. The repo is not a modelled thing, so it lives in a string.

④ THIS SESSION, 2026-09-10, unprompted and independently. Trying to draw the first-ever `CALIBRATED_AGAINST` edge — from a marker list to the corpus it was tuned against — the edge could not be drawn: `dec:calibration-is-an-edge` specifies the target as an Artifact or a Verification, and the fitting set was THE DESIGN ITSELF, which has no Artifact. Recorded in `fact:the-circular-validation-guard-has-never-had-a-single-edge-drawn`. That the same wall appeared in reflow2's own work the same day it was read in a field report is why this is worth a node.

⭐ WHAT THE FOUR HAVE IN COMMON: a file, a failure class, a repository, and a design's own export. None of them is design content the way a Requirement is; all of them are things a user genuinely wants to point AT. The cost is not only friction — it is that the graph fills with nodes nobody wanted, which then raise structural findings of their own (see the TRIGGERS link).

THE OPTIONS, none preferred:

(a) DO NOTHING. Minting a node is correct: a cause worth recording is worth a node, and a file that carries a defect probably SHOULD be registered anyway. The friction is a nudge toward modelling, not a defect. Cheapest, and it may simply be right — three of the four sightings end with a node that arguably belongs.

(b) LITERAL ENDPOINTS on specific relations — store a path or a class name on the EDGE rather than as a node. Removes the ceremony exactly where the endpoint is not design content. ⚠️ COSTS THE GRAPH INVARIANT: every walk, every propagate, every export would have to handle two kinds of endpoint, and "what does this point at" stops having one answer. That is a large price for a convenience.

(c) AUTO-REGISTER ON THE WAY — hxm's own suggestion: `record_finding(caused_by="repo:path/file.rs")` mints the Artifact and draws the edge in one call. Narrowest and cheapest to build. ⚠️ AUTO-MINTING IS THE FABRICATION RISK this project guards against elsewhere; a node created as a side effect is one nobody chose, and `dec:ask-not-repair` is the standing posture against exactly that.

(d) A LIGHTWEIGHT REFERENT TYPE — explicitly not design content, exempt from the structural detectors by construction. Answers ② directly, since a "defect class" is a referent and nothing else. ⚠️ A NEW NODE TYPE MOVES THE SCHEMA STAMP and owes a migration, and this project has just REMOVED a type (QualityGate) for not earning its place. The bar is high and this would have to clear it four times over.

🛑 THE STRONGEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it may kill the whole node: THESE MAY BE THREE PROBLEMS WEARING ONE SHAPE. A source file, a failure class, a repository and a design export are not obviously the same kind of thing — the first two are arguably real design content that simply was not registered yet, the third is deployment context, the fourth is the design's own record. A mechanism general enough to serve all four would be vague enough to serve none well, and "unify these" is the most seductive move available to somebody who has just noticed a pattern. Solving ② alone (a defect class) might be worth more than solving all four badly.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: count how many of the Artifacts in a mature consumer graph exist ONLY to be an edge endpoint — registered, carrying one inbound relation, realizing nothing anybody cares about. If that number is small, (a) holds and this is friction nobody should pay to remove.

⑤ SIGHTING FIVE, and the second independent one for ②, added 2026-09-28 from the dev_storyflow report of 2026-09-24 (art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27). Their words: "a cause that is a CLASS ('spells had no stated storage contract') has no node to point `caused_by` at until the Decision that fixes it exists — so the natural order (record cause, then decide) is inverted. I recorded the analysis as a Verification (method analysis) instead." THEIR OPPORTUNITY, as two options to add to (a)–(d) above, in their words: (e) "let `caused_by` name a Decision created in the same call"; (f) "accept a free-text class with the edge drawn later". (f) is option (b) or (d) above, restated from a second project.

⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO (e): the Decision that FIXES a class is not its cause. A CAUSES edge from the fix to the defect asserts that the fix brought the defect about, which is false. (e) would make the inversion permanent in the graph instead of removing it.

⚠️ AND A MEASURED POINT FOR (a), from the root-cause walk of this sighting (fact:root-cause-a-cause-with-no-node-yet-has-a-working-deferred-route-that-no-instruction-names-2026-09-28). On 0.72.0, record_finding with no caused_by is accepted, and create_edge CAUSES drawn later is accepted. So record-then-decide already works. What was missing was an instruction saying so. For "no stated storage contract", the root-cause skill's own Contract bone names a real endpoint: the Interface or Component whose contract is unstated. That weakens the case that a class NEEDS a new kind of endpoint, though it does not dispose of it: a class spanning several components still has nowhere to live. Recorded as brainstorming, not as a proposal; nothing here is preferred.
properties.name: OPEN — every relation needs both ends modelled, but the natural other end is often a file, a failure class or the corpus itself. Should some endpoints be literals?
properties.rationale: Four independent sightings in two days — three from hxm_program's field report (a file as a defect's cause, a failure class with nowhere to live, a repo-qualified location) and one hit unprompted in reflow2's own work when the first CALIBRATED_AGAINST edge could not be drawn because the corpus had no Artifact. The unification is this session's; the observations are the hxm agent's. Recorded as an idea rather than a proposal because the strongest counter-argument is that these are three different problems that merely rhyme, and because option (a) — the friction is a nudge toward modelling and should be paid — has not been ruled out.
